home.title: Home - Candeias
home.historyP1: Grupo Candeias de Capoeira was born in 1977 in Goiânia-GO, from an initiative by Carlinhos Chuchu at SESC Universitário. Originally called Grupo Anglo-Regional, it went through several transformations until it was consolidated under the leadership of Mestre Suíno, who structured the group on pedagogical, philosophical and cultural foundations.
home.historyP2: In 1992, it adopted the name “Candeias” and expanded across Brazil and around the world. Today it is present in 13 Brazilian states and 17 countries, with its international headquarters in Goiânia, keeping at its core the education of citizens, respect, humility and the commitment to use capoeira as a tool for social transformation.
home.philosophyQuote: “Study to improve the world, respect to be honored, work to have dignity and love to have faith”
home.locationSubtitle: Present in Brazil and around the World
home.locationText: Grupo Candeias has more than 500 centers spread across Brazil and many countries around the world, bringing the art and culture of capoeira to different communities.

history.title: Group History - Candeias
history.heading: A brief history of Grupo Candeias
history.p1: The story of Grupo Candeias de Capoeira begins in Goiás, in the late 1960s, with pioneering masters such as Sabú and Osvaldo, who planted the first seeds of capoeira in Goiânia. In 1975, then a Physical Education student, Carlinhos Chuchu saw SESC Universitário as a space for training and, with the institution's support, founded the first formal group: Grupo de Capoeira do SESC.
history.p2: Officially created in 1977 as Grupo Anglo-Regional, the group went through important transformations in the following years, with figures such as Mestre Passarinho and, above all, Mestre Suíno, who took over the leadership in 1981. Under his guidance, the group expanded through the schools and gyms of Goiânia, won the Brazilian School Games (JEBS) for six consecutive years and built its pedagogy and internal organization.
history.p3: In 1991, after an internal contest, the group adopted the name Candeias, unifying its methodology, belt system and identity. From then on a phase of major growth began, with a presence in several Brazilian states and, shortly after, in other countries across South America, Europe and North America.
history.p4: Today Grupo Candeias is present in 13 Brazilian states and in 17 countries, with its international headquarters in Goiânia (GO). Dozens of masters, instructors and students carry forward the mission of shaping citizens through capoeira, valuing culture, humility and a commitment to social transformation.
history.p5: Our motto remains our foundation: "Study to improve the world, respect to be honored, work to have dignity and love to have faith."
history.c1960p1: Capoeira in Goiás reaches its peak.
history.c1960p2: Mestre Sabú holds open rodas at Praça Cívica and at the Feira Hippie in Goiânia, spreading capoeira and selling instruments he made himself.
history.c1960p3: Mestre Osvaldo teaches at Jóquei Clube, at Colégio Carlos Chagas and at a gym in downtown Goiânia.
history.c1960p4: At the first graduation of his students, Mestre Osvaldo brings in Mestre Bimba, a historic milestone for capoeira in Goiás.
history.c1970p1: Capoeira expands through the disciples of the first masters:
history.c1970p2: Escravo, a student of Mestre Sabú, trains with friends at home and begins teaching other practitioners.
history.c1970p3: Carlinhos Chuchu (the group's future founder) is part of this class and also trains with Formiga, Mestre Bimba's son
history.c1970p4: Mestre Passarinho, self-taught, moves through these spaces but follows his own path.
history.c1975p1: Carlinhos Chuchu passes the entrance exam for Physical Education at ESEFFEGO. On his way to college, he spots SESC as a possible training space.
history.c1975p2: He proposes creating a capoeira group to the SESC Universitário coordination. The proposal is accepted, with a groundbreaking agreement:
history.c1975p3: Carlinhos' friends would receive ID cards as “Others” in order to use the space.
history.c1975p4: He could charge only the “Others”, not SESC members.
history.c1975p5: With that, the Grupo de Capoeira do SESC is born, which would become the start of the lineage of the future Grupo Candeias.
history.c1977p1: The group is formally created under the name Grupo de Capoeira Anglo‑Regional, with weekend classes at SESC Universitário.
history.c1978p1: Mestre Passarinho takes over the group and renames it Grupo São Bento Pequeno.
history.c1978p2: The group begins to grow and gain visibility in the city.
history.c1981p1: With Mestre Passarinho's departure (taking part of the students with him), the remaining group is taken over by Mestre Suíno (Elto Pereira de Brito), keeping the name Anglo-Regional for the time being
history.t1983: 1983: Capoeira at ESEFEGO and entry into the JEBS
history.c1983p1: Capoeira classes are introduced through the student council.
history.c1983p2: With Pesão's support, capoeira is included in the Brazilian School Games.
history.c1983p3: First appearance: Brazilian school champions in Campo Grande.
history.t1984: 1984-1990: Expansion, new classes and competition for space
history.c1984p1: The group begins working in the best schools and gyms in Goiânia.
history.c1984p2: A hierarchy is created with the titles of graduated student and instructor.
history.c1984p3: The group wins the JEBS for six consecutive years.
history.c1984p4: Capoeira is included in the Goiânia School Games.
history.t1991: 1991-1992: Unification and the birth of the name “Candeias”
history.c1991p1: An internal contest defines the group's name: "Candeias".
history.c1991p2: The organizational structure now has six areas: historical-cultural, technical, musical, philosophical, pedagogical and administrative.
history.c1991p3: Uniform, belt system and the naming of movements are unified.
history.t1995: 1995-2000: Expansion in Goiânia and to other states
history.c1995p1: The group has more than 20 teachers in Goiânia.
history.c1995p2: New members in Anápolis, in the interior of Goiás and in other states.
history.c1995p3: Teachers such as Soneca, Grilo, Cariri, Besouro and others join Candeias.
history.t1996: 1996-2000: Consolidation in São Paulo and international expansion
history.c1996p1: Teachers Gaguinho, Saliba, Nadú, Pardal and others join the group.
history.c1996p2: Guerreiro consolidates the work in São Paulo (Osasco, Cotia, Itapevi and others).
history.c1996p3: The group establishes itself in Peru, then in Chile, Argentina, Colombia, Ecuador and Bolivia.
history.c2000p1: Group capoeiristas settle abroad: USA, Portugal, Spain, Italy, England, Czech Republic.
history.c2000p2: International headquarters of Associação Candeias in Goiânia.
history.c2000p3: Participation in cultural shows, dance and theater in Brazil and abroad.
history.c2000p4: Release of 4 CDs, books, booklets and DVDs.
history.c2000p5: Launch of the Open Candeias Internacional and the Encontro Pedagógico.
history.c2012p1: Open Candeias editions alternate yearly between Brazil and abroad.
history.c2012p2: The Goiás identity is reinforced as the central headquarters (code GYN).
history.c2012p3: The group is present in 13 Brazilian states and in 17 countries.
history.c2012p4: 21 active masters, with 4 more expected to graduate in 2019.

conselho.title: Council of Masters - Candeias
conselho.grau2: Masters - 2nd DEGREE - red and white cord
conselho.suinoHistoria: Born on June 4, 1963, in Santa Helena de Goiás (GO). He began practicing at the age of 14, at SESC Setor Universitário in Goiânia. He holds a degree in Physical Education (ESEFFEGO/GO) and a postgraduate degree in School Physical Education. He graduated as a Capoeira Master in 1980, the first master graduated by Grupo Candeias. He is a five-time Goiás state capoeira champion (2000–2005, 2007).
